cues.en: All right.
In this video we are going to walk through how pivot function is going to work.
And it's going to be a helper function to be able to create the quicksort algorithm.
So to explain it we are just going to put our list like this.
And in the previous lecture we have explained how pivot works in case of quicksort.
So first we are selecting the first number as a pivot.
Then the aim over here is we are just going to put all numbers that are less than the pivot on the left,
and all numbers that are greater than the pivot on the right.
So this is the aim that we need to reach when we are writing the pivot function.
So at the end our main list will look like this.
So in this case all numbers that are less than three is on the left.
And all numbers that are greater than three are on the right.
Then we are doing the same operation for the left list and for the right list.
Now in this case, I'm going to put everything back and to show you how we will walk through this list
to make the pivot function work.
So first thing over here we need to find out the pivot number.
And as we mentioned before, the private number will be the first number in our list.
So in our case it is three.
Then we are going to compare it with everything after the private number.
The numbers that we have over here within a loop.
And the loop is going to start from the first number after the private number.
So in this case inside the loop we will have a variable which is going to be I.
So that's why I'm going to put I over here in the starting point of the loop.
So we are not going to start from the private number.
We are going to start after the private number.
Then I'm going to put the pivot point.
So it's obvious that the pivot point will be like this.
Then we will have another variable which is going to help us to swap the values.
So in this case this swap index also will start from the pivot number.
So here we have the pivot index.
And here we have the swap index.
Then the next thing that we are going to do we are going to continue the standard operation for the
pivot.
So this means that we are going to compare all numbers one by one.
And in this case, to make it more understandable, we are changing the color.
So five is greater than three.
So this means that we are just going to change the color of the five to yellow.
Then we will continue to the next number.
Now the next number is zero, and zero is less than three.
So we are going to change the color to blue.
Then when we face the number which is less than the private number, we are swapping it with the first
number that is greater than the pivot.
Now, to be able to find that number, all we have to do is whenever we are facing in I index the number
that is smaller than the pivot, we are going to move the swap index also.
Now swap index stays in the first number that is greater than the pivot number.
And we have faced it with the number that is smaller than the pivot number.
So in this case we are going to swap the values that we have in these indexes over here.
So we are going to swap it.
And we are going to continue to loop through this list.
So I will continue to the next number.
So in this case the next number is six which is greater than three.
And we are going to just set it to yellow.
So as you can see whenever we are facing with the number which is greater than the pivot number, we
are not moving the swap value.
Then we are going to continue to the next number.
In the next number we have two, which is less than the three.
So we are making it blue and we need to move the swap index also.
So swap index will move to the five.
Then we are going to swap them.
Now after swapping it the operation will continue.
Then we are going to continue to the next number.
So this number is one which is less than three.
Then one more time when we are facing the number which is less than the pivot number, we have to move
the swap value.
So we are moving swap value over here.
Then we are going to swap the the value that is located in the swap index with the I index.
Then we are continuing to the next number.
So the next number is four.
So in this case four is greater than three.
So this means that we are just going to mark it yellow.
Then we have done with the I index.
So I'm just going to remove the I index from here.
And we will stick with this pivot index and swap index.
Then the next thing that we are going to do we are going to swap the values that is located in the swap
index with the pivot index.
So to be able to do that we are going to swap it like this.
Then after swapping it we have done with the pivot index.
So I'm just going to take it out the pivot index, then we have only swap index.
Now our pivot function will return the index of the this swap index.
Now you might be interested why it is not returning the pivot number.
It is just returning the index.
So we are going to need it to be able to continue to our next operation.
So in the next case, we know that we are going to continue to the left side of the list and the right
side of the list.
Now to be able to get the numbers on the left side, we are going to start from the first index until
the swap index, and we are not going to include the swap index.
And for the right side of the list, we are going to start from the swap plus one index.
We are not going to include the swap because we have considered these three numbers as ordered.
So that's why it's not going to be included.
We are going to start from swap index plus one until the end of the list.
So it will continue like this.
So that's why whenever we are writing the pivot function it's going to return the these numbers index
not the number itself.
It's going to return the index.
So that's how the pivot function will work.
Now in the next lecture we are going to go ahead and implement this one in practice.
